Italy’s Industrial Output Rises in July, Signaling Manufacturing Recovery

  • by Lauren Jacobs
  • October 10, 2025

Italian industrial output grew by 0.4% in July, surprising economists and suggesting renewed strength in the country’s long-struggling manufacturing sector.

Italy's industrial output unexpectedly rose by 0. 4% in July compared with the previous month providing a fresh sign of recovery for the manufacturing sector Analysts had anticipated a 0.

1% decline making this the second consecutive positive surprise following June’s 0. 2% growth According to ISTAT all major industry groups contributed to the increase except for energy On a work day-adjusted year-on-year basis output was up 0.

9% in July reversing the 0. 7% decrease in June Earlier surveys including a PMI report indicated that Italian manufacturing returned to growth in August after sixteen months of contraction This positive momentum reflects underlying resilience in production capacity investment trends and domestic demand despite lingering challenges in supply chains and global economic conditions The manufacturing sector in Italy has long been a central driver of the national economy representing a significant portion of GDP employment and exports Sustained improvements in industrial output suggest that firms may be adjusting successfully to post-pandemic supply chain disruptions energy cost fluctuations and shifts in consumer demand patterns Analysts highlight that the surprise growth in July signals cautious optimism among industrial producers and may provide an early indication that targeted government policies investment incentives and support measures are having an effect The composition of the output increase is particularly important as it encompasses multiple sub-sectors including machinery automotive textiles chemicals and consumer goods The exception of the energy sector in contributing to the growth may reflect ongoing challenges in energy supply costs regulatory constraints and the transition toward more sustainable and renewable sources Nevertheless the overall industrial recovery indicates adaptive capacity and potential for stabilization of production trends Work day-adjusted year-on-year comparisons provide additional insight into structural performance accounting for variations in calendar effects and allowing for a more precise understanding of underlying growth patterns The 0.

9% increase in July compared to the previous year not only reverses June's contraction but also signals that manufacturers are experiencing improved operational conditions potentially including increased orders export demand and inventory replenishment The role of business confidence surveys such as purchasing managers indexes PMI reinforces this narrative by capturing expectations production activity new orders employment and supplier deliveries Surveys indicating that Italian manufacturing returned to growth in August after a prolonged period of contraction reflect both cyclical and structural shifts in industrial performance providing further evidence of sectoral resilience While the industrial output data offers encouraging signs for manufacturing the broader economic outlook in Italy remains subject to uncertainty Macroeconomic indicators including gross domestic product GDP suggest that the economy is facing multiple headwinds from global trade tensions geopolitical risks fluctuating energy prices and domestic consumption trends Italy's GDP contracted by 0. 1% in the second quarter reflecting persistent weaknesses in investment spending private consumption and export growth Despite this contraction the government maintains a forecast for 0.
